files.purpose: Configure Jac 0.36.1 [project] name rentora-backend, kind service and entry-point main.jac; this headless slice has no npm or AI dependencies.

Define enums EventType {MAINTENANCE, PAYMENT, LEASE, COMPLAINT, INQUIRY} and UrgencyLevel {LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL} with sem descriptions per member. Nodes with defaulted fields: Property(name, address, city, state, zip_code: str=""); Unit(number:str="", bedrooms:int=1, bathrooms:int=1, sq_ft:int=0, status:str="occupied"); Lease(start_date, end_date: str="", rent_amount:float=0.0, deposit:float=0.0, status:str="active"); Tenant(name, phone, email: str="", payment_status:str="current", move_in_date:str=""); Ticket(ticket_id, category, description: str="", urgency:str="medium", status:str="open", ai_summary, ai_diagnosis, recommended_action, tenant_reply, owner_alert, created_at, resolved_at, vendor_name: str="", estimated_cost:float=0.0); Vendor(name, category, phone, email: str="", rating:float=0.0, avg_cost:float=0.0, available:bool=True). Edges HasUnit, HasLease, HasTenant, HasTicket, AssignedTo (no fields) and Services(jobs_completed:int=0, total_spent:float=0.0, last_service_date:str=""). Graph shape: root -> Property -HasUnit-> Unit -HasLease-> Lease -HasTenant-> Tenant; Unit -HasTicket-> Ticket; Property -Services-> Vendor.

signatures.EventType: enum EventType { MAINTENANCE, PAYMENT, LEASE, COMPLAINT, INQUIRY }
signatures.UrgencyLevel: enum UrgencyLevel { LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL }
signatures.Property: node Property { has name: str = ""; has address: str = ""; has city: str = ""; has state: str = ""; has zip_code: str = ""; }
signatures.Unit: node Unit { has number: str = ""; has bedrooms: int = 1; has bathrooms: int = 1; has sq_ft: int = 0; has status: str = "occupied"; }
signatures.Lease: node Lease { has start_date: str = ""; has end_date: str = ""; has rent_amount: float = 0.0; has deposit: float = 0.0; has status: str = "active"; }
signatures.Tenant: node Tenant { has name: str = ""; has phone: str = ""; has email: str = ""; has payment_status: str = "current"; has move_in_date: str = ""; }
signatures.Ticket: node Ticket { has ticket_id: str = ""; has category: str = ""; has description: str = ""; has urgency: str = "medium"; has status: str = "open"; has ai_summary: str = ""; has ai_diagnosis: str = ""; has recommended_action: str = ""; has tenant_reply: str = ""; has owner_alert: str = ""; has created_at: str = ""; has resolved_at: str = ""; has vendor_name: str = ""; has estimated_cost: float = 0.0; }
signatures.Vendor: node Vendor { has name: str = ""; has category: str = ""; has phone: str = ""; has email: str = ""; has rating: float = 0.0; has avg_cost: float = 0.0; has available: bool = True; }
signatures.Services: edge Services { has jobs_completed: int = 0; has total_spent: float = 0.0; has last_service_date: str = ""; }

files.purpose: Local SQLite log store using Python stdlib only (os getcwd, os.path join, sqlite3 connect, json dumps/loads, datetime). glob _db_path = <cwd>/.jac/data/app.db and glob _tables_ready flag; private _ensure_tables() creates sms_messages, walker_logs and notifications tables once. Public helpers insert and query those tables, plus a generic db_insert/db_find keyed by collection; each catches exceptions and returns a failure dict or empty list. check_db_health() ensures tables and returns {ok:True, backend:"sqlite", path, tables:[names]} or {ok:False, backend:"sqlite", path} on error.

files.purpose: Import Property, Unit, Lease, Tenant, Ticket, Vendor, HasUnit, HasLease, HasTenant, HasTicket, Services from services.graph.models and check_db_health from services.graph.localdb. list_properties reports ONE list of dicts {id: jid(p), name, address, city, state, unit_count} for each Property on root. list_units visits each Property and reports one dict per HasUnit unit {id, unit, bedrooms, bathrooms, sq_ft, status, property, tenant, tenant_phone, payment_status, rent, lease_end, open_tickets, total_tickets} using the first lease/tenant if any. list_tickets visits Property -> HasUnit units and reports one dict per HasTicket ticket {id, ticket_id, unit, category, description, urgency, status, ai_summary, recommended_action, vendor_name, estimated_cost, tenant_reply, owner_alert, created_at, resolved_at}. list_vendors reports one dict per Services-linked Vendor. register_tenant skips properties whose name differs from a non-empty property_name, finds a unit by case-insensitive number or creates Unit(number=upper), reports {status:"already_registered", tenant, phone, unit, property, id} and disengages if a tenant with the same phone is under that unit's leases, otherwise creates Lease (deposit = rent) and Tenant via HasLease/HasTenant and reports {status:"registered", tenant, phone, unit, property, id} then disengages. db_health reports {database: check_db_health(), graph_store:"ok"}. list_tenants reports ONE list of {id, full_name, phone_number, unit_number, property_id, property_name, rent, lease_end}. add_property_node attaches Property(name, address) to root with one HasUnit Unit per unit number and reports {status:"created", id, property, units}. delete_tenant_node deletes the tenant whose jid matches and reports {status:"deleted"}, else on Root exit {status:"not_found", tenant_id}. delete_property_node deletes a root Property by jid and reports {status:"deleted"}, else {status:"not_found"}. match_tenant reports {matched:True, tenant_name, property_name, unit} for the first tenant with that phone, else on Root exit {matched:False}.

signatures.list_properties: walker list_properties { can list_all with Root entry; }
signatures.list_units: walker list_units { can start with Root entry; can gather with Property entry; }
signatures.list_tickets: walker list_tickets { can start with Root entry; can at_property with Property entry; can at_unit with Unit entry; }
signatures.list_vendors: walker list_vendors { can start with Root entry; can at_property with Property entry; }
signatures.register_tenant: walker register_tenant { has tenant_name: str = ""; has tenant_phone: str = ""; has tenant_email: str = ""; has unit_number: str = ""; has rent_amount: float = 0.0; has lease_start: str = ""; has lease_end: str = ""; has property_name: str = ""; can start with Root entry; can find_unit with Property entry; }
signatures.db_health: walker db_health { can check with Root entry; }
signatures.list_tenants: walker list_tenants { can list_all with Root entry; }
signatures.add_property_node: walker add_property_node { has name: str = ""; has address: str = ""; has unit_numbers: list = []; can create with Root entry; }
signatures.delete_tenant_node: walker delete_tenant_node { has tenant_id: str = ""; can start with Root entry; can at_property with Property entry; can not_found with Root exit; }
signatures.delete_property_node: walker delete_property_node { has property_id: str = ""; can start with Root entry; }
signatures.match_tenant: walker match_tenant { has phone: str = ""; can start with Root entry; can at_property with Property entry; can not_found with Root exit; }

files.purpose: Import datetime and Property, Unit, Ticket, HasUnit, HasTicket from services.graph.models. Both walkers visit root Properties, then HasUnit units, then scan HasTicket tickets for ticket_id == self.ticket_id. approve_dispatch sets status "dispatched" and reports {ticket_id, status:"dispatched", vendor_name, unit: here.number, tenant_reply, owner_alert, estimated_cost} then disengages. resolve_ticket sets status "resolved" and resolved_at = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), reports {ticket_id, status:"resolved", resolved_at} then disengages.

signatures.approve_dispatch: walker approve_dispatch { has ticket_id: str = ""; can start with Root entry; can at_property with Property entry; can at_unit with Unit entry; }
signatures.resolve_ticket: walker resolve_ticket { has ticket_id: str = ""; can start with Root entry; can at_property with Property entry; can at_unit with Unit entry; }

files.purpose: Entry point with a module docstring that only re-exports: import list_properties, list_units, list_tickets, list_vendors, register_tenant, db_health, list_tenants, add_property_node, delete_tenant_node, delete_property_node, match_tenant from services.graph.crud and approve_dispatch, resolve_ticket from services.graph.actions. No other code.

verify.flow: add property -> register tenant -> list/match -> attach ticket -> dispatch -> resolve -> delete property
